tāyana.notes: In SN 2.8 Tāyana recites to the Buddha at night. The Buddha repeats the verses to the monks after Tāyana leaves. SN 2.10 mentions him only in the chapter recap.

udaya.notes: DPD's ascetic is Bāvarī’s pupil, named in Snp 5.1 and 5.18 and speaking in Snp 5.14. His entry is missing. Udaya 01 describes the Sāvatthī brahmin who fills the Buddha’s bowl three times in SN 7.12. Udaya himself takes refuge there. SN 7.11 concerns Bhāradvāja the farmer.

udena.notes: AN 8.70, DN 16, DN 24, SN 51.10 and Ud 6.1 name the Udena shrine at Vesālī, which has no candidate. Ud 7.10 also names the king in the account of Sāmāvatī’s death, under the separate DPD spelling utena (rañño utenassa). SN 35.125–126 and MN 93 are neighboring page matches.

udumbarikā.notes: DN 25 calls the place Udumbarikā’s monastery for wanderers. The identification of its benefactor as a queen comes from the commentary.

udāyī.notes: Udāyī 01 explicitly names Paṇḍita Udāyī in the Pañcakaṅga dialogue. AN 1.225 names Kāḷudāyī as foremost at inspiring families. Thag 15.2 attributes the elephant verses to Udāyī Thera, while Thag 10.1 separately names Kāḷudāyī. AN 6.43 repeats the elephant verses under the short name. DPD and the alternative attribution recorded by DPPN give them to Kāḷudāyī, so that discourse is unresolved. DPPN's links to DN 28 and MN 66 are commentarial. MN 77 and MN 79 address the wanderer Sakuludāyī. AN 5.166, AN 6.29, AN 9.34, AN 9.42 and MN 136 give insufficient evidence to distinguish the monks. AN 6.30 and SN 35.237 have recap mentions only. AN 4.39 concerns the brahmin Ujjaya. The neighboring page matches AN 3.81, AN 5.158 and 5.160, AN 6.42, AN 9.36, MN 58 and 65, SN 35.132, SN 36.18 and SN 46.25 and 46.29 supply no Udāyī episode.

ugga.notes: DPD's minister example names a member of King Eḷeyya’s retinue. Ugga 02 is the chief minister in AN 7.7, where the hundred thousand in gold belongs to Migāra. AN 1.253 names the donor of Vesālī and AN 1.254 names the attendant of Hatthigāma. Both share one packet ID. AN 6.120–139 likewise lists them on consecutive lines (1.6–7), so neither group can have one preferred entry. The shared page citations cross between the two householders. AN 1.258–267, AN 1.268–277, AN 5.43, AN 7.6, AN 8.20 and AN 9.42–43 contain none of the cited Ugga episodes.

uggatasarīra.notes: The sacrifice, Ānanda’s intervention and Uggatasarīra’s release of the animals are in AN 7.47. The entry’s reference lands in AN 9.34, a conversation between Sāriputta and Udāyī about extinguishment.

ujjaya.notes: The monk’s attribution is at Thag 1.47. The TH50 hint comes from the chapter recap at Thag 1.50, where Ujjaya is joined to Samiddhi and Sañjaya. DPPN’s verse 67 belongs to Ekadhammasavanīya. In AN 8.55 the brahmin says he intends to travel (pavāsaṁ gantukāmā), where DPPN describes a retreat (upavāsa). AN 4.38 and AN 8.54 are neighboring page matches. In AN 4.40 and AN 8.60 Ujjaya appears only in the chapter recap.

ujjenī.notes: Snp 5.1 names Ujjenī on the students’ route and Thig 15.1 names it as Isidāsī’s home. The placed citations are indirect. DN 19 calls Māhissatī the Avanti capital, MN 108 mentions King Pajjota, and MN 107 shares the cited page.

ujjuhāna.notes: The DPD sense and the entry both preserve two interpretations of the simile in Thag 11.1. Sujato takes ujjuhāno as a bird. The hill is a commentarial interpretation.

ukkaṭṭhā.notes: AN 4.36 names the road to Setavyā and MN 49 sets the Baka episode in the Subhaga forest at Ukkaṭṭhā. The parallel in SN 6.4 begins at Jeta’s Grove in Sāvatthī. AN 4.35 and SN 6.3 also lack the town.

upaka.notes: Upaka 01 covers both the Ājīvaka on the road and the Upaka freed in Avihā. The link between those stages of his life is traditional. MN 26 and MN 85 place the meeting on the way to Isipatana, reversing the entry’s opening direction. In SN 1.50 and SN 2.24 Ghaṭīkāra reports the liberation of seven, including Upaka. The entry describes this as a visit by the seven. AN 4.188 names Maṇḍikā’s son. AN 4.187 and 4.189 are page neighbors.

upananda.notes: MN 116 gives twelve Ānandas, Nandas and Upanandas in all. DPD and DPPN specify four Upanandas. The Sakyan monk of the Vinaya has no candidate here.
